newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Alpha still hopeful on Blue Circle merger.
newsitem.headline: Alpha still hopeful on Blue Circle merger.

text.p: South African cement group Alpha Ltd said on Wednesday it was still hopeful its planned tie-up with rival Blue Circle would go ahead despite a recommended veto from the Competition Board.

Executives from Alpha and Blue Circle, which is owned by Murray and Roberts Holdings Ltd, will meet with Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin within the next two weeks to try and persuade him to give the deal the green light.
"The Competition Board (recommendation) is a knock back, but we do not view the door as being closed," said Rowan Dent, Alpha director of corporate communications.
The merger, if it goes ahead, will create a sector dominated by two large players -- Alpha-Blue Circle with 55 percent of the market and Pretoria Portland Cement Co Ltd (PPC) with 45 percent.

Dent told Reuters the move would not hit competition. "Our main point, that we feel very strongly, is that competition between two more-or-less equally strong firms will be better than the present fragmented market," he said.
However, most analysts were sceptical about any possibility Erwin would go against the board. "The chances are about zero of this going ahead," said one.

One analyst warned this could be bad for the industry as without consolidation it would be difficult for firms to get economies of scale and cut the cost of production. This could prevent the cement price from dropping and make it difficult to compete abroad.
Officials at the Department of Trade and Industry were not available for comment.
The Competition Board said in its recommendation last week it was not convinced the merger was in the public interest.

"With little prospect of new rivals entering the market as well as the negligible threat of imports, there were insufficient market pressures after the merger to ensure that these efficiencies would filter through to benefit end users," it said.

The saga, that began in June when the firms first announced merger plans, took a new twist on Wednesday with news that Alpha was reconsidering a planned 800 million rand cement plant at Saldanha in the Western Cape -- a PPC stronghold.

"The fact of the matter is that we always wanted to go ahead in the Western Cape in a merged structure to get more financial muscle...(the Competition Board recommendation) puts it in a different light," Dent said.

But Alpha does still intend to enter the Western Cape even if the merger, and possibly the Saldanha plant and the 400 jobs it would create, fall through. "Our objective remains to enter the market. How we get there is another matter," Dent said.
Dent said he expected Erwin to make a decision soon after his meetings with the firms.
If Erwin decides to give the merger the go-ahead it could be delayed by a referral back to the Competition Board.

Should the minister agree with the board, Alpha and Blue Circle could appeal, but Dent said the firms would be unlikely to embark on such a drawn out process. "I don't think any purpose would be served by that," he said.
At 1335 GMT Alpha shares were up 25 cents at 92.25 rand and Murray & Roberts down 15 cents to 17 rand.
